comment: D-SINK-19. state.json's `activeKey`: which source is active, by key, in the
plugin's own 0600 file instead of as a provider URL in the host's shell.json.
Run by BOTH tests/Model.test.js and tests/test_state.py, because the rule is
implemented twice -- Model.activeKeyText / parseState in QML JS, and
normalize_active_key / normalize_state in the helper -- and a rule in two
languages gets one fixture (engineering rule 12, dev branch). The helper is the
half that matters most here: it REBUILDS the document from default_state() and
copies the keys it knows, so a key it has not been taught is ERASED by the next
`state favorite add`, and for THIS key that means the plugin reads as not
configured at all. savedSearches and hiddenGroups both carry that warning; this
one would have been visible.
Sections, and who runs each. A name here that is not a key of this file is the
join rule 13 warns about, and Model.test.js checks the list against the keys:
`parse`   BOTH. The raw JSON value of `activeKey` and the string both readers
must produce. A key naming no record is KEPT at parse time on
purpose: whether it resolves is a property of the LIST, not of the
value (Model.activeKeyOf is where the resolution happens).
`remove`  BOTH. Removing a source: the pointer the state is left with
(Model.removeSource and the helper's remove_source_record, R3).
`resolve` JavaScript only. Model.activeKeyOf over a stored key and a list.
`adopt`   JavaScript only. Model.adoptActiveSource's ORDER (lead ruling R1):
a URL the plan adopts first, then the state's key, then the
entry's mirror, then nothing; the guide URL rules (R4, R21c) and
the migration marker (R21a). The helper never resolves the active
source and never migrates one: the migration reads the host's bar
entry and the helper knows nothing about shell.json by design (D15).
`order`   JavaScript only. Model.pointerWritePlan (R5): state before entry,
and the entry waits for a parked state save.
`reload`  JavaScript only. Model.reloadDisposition (D-SRC-15, R9): a reload of
state.json never replaces in-memory state newer than the file.
`flush`   JavaScript only. Model.entryFlushDisposition (D-SRC-15, R11): the
held entry mirror is written only once the parked save has
LANDED and the helper's start-up init exited 0; else dropped.
recordsNote: The records `adopt` and `remove` build states from, by key. A case's `keys` list names which of them the state carries; `new` below is a URL none of them has, whose key is d5977d8a.

parse.name: absent reads as no active source
a three-digit suffix is the widest the grammar admits
surrounding whitespace is trimmed, not refused
an empty string is no active source
uppercase hex is not a key (the writers emit lowercase)
seven hex characters is not a key
nine hex characters is not a key
a four-digit suffix is not a key
a path traversal is not a key, which is what keeps it out of a directory name
a slash is not a key
a key with an interior space is not a key
a URL is not a key, and this is the shape a hand-edited old file would carry
a number is not a key
a boolean is not a key
a list is not a key
an object is not a key

resolveNote: Model.activeKeyOf: the stored key, but only while it names a record the same state carries. The dangling cases are the ones a CLI `state source remove`, an eviction and a hand-edited file all produce.

resolve.name: dangling: the record it named is gone
not a key, with a record that would otherwise match nothing

adoptNote: Each case: a state (`keys`, `activeKey`, and `migrated` for a state whose memory already carries the migration marker), the bar entry as settingsFrom read it, the plan's flags (`migrating`, `adoptUrl`, `adoptEpg`; each false when absent -- a caller with no plan reads no URL, R21b), and what adoptActiveSource must answer. `sources` is the count the state comes out with; `epgOnActive` is the active record's epgUrl afterwards; `migrated` whether the result carries the marker. Round 11 (R21) withdrew the pending-guide-URL and set-time cases (R19b, R19c): a guide URL with no source to guide is `noSourceEpg`, reported and stripped, never held.

adopt.name: R1 step 1: a fresh URL beside a resolving key -- the URL is adopted, added, and the key MOVES (the review's P1: the first version returned the key and discarded the URL)
R1 step 1: a fresh KNOWN URL beside a different active key -- that record becomes active, nothing is added
R1 step 1: the same URL again (re-set by the user) -- active already, nothing moves, the entry is still rewritten to take the URL out
R1 step 1 refused: an invalid URL beside a resolving key -- the key is kept exactly as it was and the refusal is reported (D16)
R1 step 1 refused, with no active source at all: the refusal is the only thing there is
R1 step 1, the old shape: a URL on the entry and no key anywhere -- the migration
R1 step 1 over a dangling state key: the URL is adopted and the dangling value replaced
R1 step 2: no URL, a resolving state key -- the key, and nothing to write
R1 step 2: the state's key beats a DIFFERENT mirror on the entry, and the mirror is rewritten
R1 step 3: no URL, no state key, the entry's sourceKey names a record -- the mirror recovers it
R1 step 3: a mirror naming a record that is gone is not a pointer
R1 step 3: a non-key on the entry is not a pointer
R1 step 4: nothing anywhere -- a dangling state key is CLEARED, not left for the next reader
R1 step 4: an empty install stays empty and writes nothing
R1 consumed: a URL the service already adopted (the host's stale echo, rule 9) is NOT read -- the key wins, and the entry is rewritten because the URL is still on it
R1 consumed, over NO state key: the stale echo does not resurrect a source the user removed through the CLI
R4: a fresh EPG input alone reaches the ACTIVE record (D-SRC-02), and the entry is rewritten to take it out
R4: a consumed EPG input is not adopted twice
R4: an EPG input the record already holds changes nothing
R4: an invalid EPG input is not adopted, and still asks for the entry write that takes it out
R21c: a guide URL with no source to guide is NOT held -- noSourceEpg (reported and stripped by the entry write it asks for); R12 left it on the entry and R19b in the state, and both were withdrawn
R1+R4: a fresh URL and a fresh EPG in one write land on the record the URL named
D-SRC-10 kept: a fresh URL beside a CONSUMED EPG -- the EPG was the previous source's and does not follow
R1+R4 at the migration with no source yet: a URL and a guide URL on one entry land together on the record the URL adds
R21c: a guide URL beside a REFUSED playlist with no source: both reported (invalid, noSourceEpg), nothing held, one write takes both out
R21c: a REFUSED guide URL with no source is a guide URL with no source -- noSourceEpg, nothing held, written out (rule 5)
R18a: a guide URL of control characters alone with no source is NO input: no report, nothing changes, and the entry write still takes the junk out
R21a: the migration of a 0.13.x state -- the URL the entry names becomes active, and the SAME result carries the marker (it rides the state write the adoption makes)
R21a: the migration of an install whose entry carries nothing: the marker is set all the same, so a URL set on the entry later is refused
R21a: an empty install migrates too -- no source, the marker, and nothing to write to the entry
R21a: a second migration reconcile over memory that already carries the marker (the save has not landed yet) -- the same URL again moves nothing and marks nothing
R21a: an INVALID URL at the migration is reported (D16) and the marker is set anyway -- the value is stripped once the write lands, never adopted later
R21b: after the marker, the plan adopts nothing -- a URL on the entry is not read, the state's key answers, and the entry write that strips it is asked for
R21b: no plan at all reads no URL -- the safe default for a caller that forgot it, a NEW url on the entry included

removeNote: Each case: the records the state carries, its activeKey, the key removed, and the pointer and count the state is left with. `ok` false is an unknown key: no change on either side (the helper reports unknown_source).

remove.name: R3: removing the ACTIVE record clears the pointer
R3: removing an INACTIVE record leaves the pointer alone
R3: removing the only record, which is active
R3: removing with no active source changes nothing about the pointer
R3: an unknown key removes nothing and moves nothing

orderNote: Model.pointerWritePlan: the two writes a pointer change makes, in order. `keyMoved` is whether the state's key changes in this call; `dirsReady` and `savePending` are the service's start-up gate (saveState parks a write until stateInitProc has made the 0600 file); `savesInFlight` is setText calls not yet confirmed by `saved` and `saveFailed` whether the last write failed (R13, 2026-10-12). The entry NEVER goes out ahead of a state save that has not LANDED: `write-entry` only when nothing of ours is outstanding, `write-entry-after-saved` / `wait-entry` hold the key for Model.entryFlushDisposition. `entryWaits` is true whenever the entry is held.

order.name: R5/R13: the key moved and the dirs are ready -- state now, the entry once that save LANDS (round-3 review P1: it used to go out straight after setText)
R5: the key moved before the dirs are ready -- the state save parks and the entry WAITS for it (the interrupted-migration case)
R5/R13: the key moved, dirs ready, an earlier save still parked -- the save flushes first and the entry waits for it to land
R13: the key moved, dirs ready, another write already in flight -- the same held answer
R5: the key did not move but an earlier save is parked behind the dirs -- the entry waits
R5/R13: the key did not move, an earlier save is parked, dirs ready -- flush it, then the entry once it lands (nothing else would wake a wait)

R13 (the round-3 P1): the key did not move, nothing parked, a save IN FLIGHT -- adoptActive saved and persistActive reached this through Qt.callLater with the key already in memory; the entry waits for that save to land
R13: the key did not move, nothing in flight, the LAST save FAILED -- held, and the disposition drops it at once: the file is older than memory and the URL on the entry is the only copy
R13: in flight AND the last one failed (two writes, the first failed) -- held
R5: nothing of ours outstanding -- the entry, now
R5: nothing to save and dirs not ready -- the file already says what memory says, the entry may go
R13: a non-numeric in-flight count reads as nothing in flight (the service's property is an int; a missing one is not a save)
R5: no input at all is the cautious no-move, dirs-not-ready answer

reloadNote: Model.reloadDisposition (D-SRC-15, R9): whether a reload of state.json is applied over the in-memory state. `loadedBefore` is stateLoaded, `ownWrite` whether the text is one this service wrote (recentSaves), `savePending` the save parked behind the start-up dirs, `savesInFlight` setText calls not yet confirmed by `saved`, `saveFailed` whether the last write failed. The file is older than memory in every `ignore` case and the parked or in-flight save overwrites it anyway. R24a (D-SINK-19 round 14, D-SRC-22): `matchesBase` is whether the text is the disk as the service last knew it (Model.sameState of the text and Service.landedState, the BASE). Held (parked, in flight or failed) and matching the base, a reload is ignored for the reason it is held, as R9 had it -- the start-up chmod reload carries the file as loaded, so the D-SRC-15 cases carry matchesBase true; held and NOT matching the base it is a FOREIGN write and is MERGED (Model.mergeForeignState), reason foreign-<why held>, never ignored and never applied blind. With nothing held a reload is applied (file-newer), base or not: that is the merge with ours == base.

reload.name: the first load always applies: memory is the empty default plus a replay
the first load applies even with a save parked (a play before the load; stateOnLoad replays it)
our own write echoed back is skipped (player design R10)
D-SRC-15: the start-up chmod reload while the adoption's save is PARKED -- ignored; the parked save writes memory over the file
D-SRC-15 sibling: an IPC switch or remove before dirsReady parks a save -- the same flag, the same answer
a reload while a write is in flight (setText returned, saved has not fired) is ignored
two writes in flight: still ignored
the last write FAILED and the file is still what we last knew: applying it would replay the loss
nothing of ours outstanding: a foreign write (the CLI) is applied
R24a: a FOREIGN write while a save is PARKED (a hand-run helper verb inside the start-up window) is merged, not ignored
R24a: a FOREIGN write while one of ours is IN FLIGHT is merged
R24a / D-SRC-22: a FOREIGN write after a write FAILED (the data-loss lens's HADD after WF) is merged, so the next save keeps both
R24a: a held change and a context that does not say the text is the base reads as foreign and is merged (ignoring is what lost the helper's write)
R24a: our own write echoed back is skipped even when it is not the base (it is newer than the base)
R24a: nothing held and the text is the base (an identical rewrite, a chmod): applied, the identity
a missing context reads as a first load

flushNote: Model.entryFlushDisposition (D-SRC-15, R11): whether the entry mirror that waited for a parked state save (pointerWritePlan `wait-entry`, held in pendingEntryKey) is written now. `initOk` is the helper's start-up `state init` exit code read as 0; the save has LANDED when nothing is parked or in flight and the last write did not fail. A `drop` leaves the entry as it is: the URL on it is the only copy of a source whose state write did not land.

flush.name: held, dirs not ready yet: wait (stateInitProc has not exited)
R11: the helper's init FAILED -- the entry is not rewritten, the URL stays as the backup
R11: the parked save FAILED to land -- the entry is not rewritten
R11: the parked save was issued and is in flight -- wait for `saved`, setText returning is not the write succeeding
still parked (saveState not yet run): wait
landed: the mirror is written, and only now
a cleared pointer (removeSource before the dirs were ready) is a key to flush like any other
R13: the last save FAILED but a new one is IN FLIGHT -- wait for its own verdict; checked the other way round a switch after any earlier failure dropped its mirror before its write reported
R13: the last save failed and another is PARKED -- wait; the parked one reports when issued
R11 still: init failed outranks a save in flight (R11 as ruled: the mirror needs init 0 AND the save landed)
R22a: the no-write mode drops a held key even with a save in flight (no write will land to wait for; the entry is left as it is)
R22a: the no-write mode drops a held key before the dirs are ready too
R22a: nothing held is still nothing, blocked or not

ownedWriteNote: R16 (D-SINK-19 round 5, amended round 6): Model.ownedWriteMode over the FOUR inputs an owned-entry write that is NOT the key mirror is handed: stateLoaded and the three save flags. `patch` before the first state load (memory is still emptyState, so the toggle would mirror sourceKey "" and strip a URL set while the shell was down -- the round-5 data-loss lens, 3 of 4 host/disk combinations) and whenever a state write is parked, in flight or failed (the file is older than memory and the URL on the entry may be the only copy, so the write carries showLogos alone and leaves sourceKey and the retired URL keys as the host publishes them -- on the lagging host one write behind, D-SINK-20); `heal` only when the state is loaded and nothing of ours is outstanding. The reason names the input that decided: state-not-loaded first, then the save flags in the order entryFlushDisposition reads them. R22a (round 12) adds a FIFTH input, `blocked` (the no-write mode's reason, "" when writes are allowed), checked first: while a state.json that did not load holds the service in the no-write mode the answer is `none` -- no owned entry write at all, the patch included, because the entry may hold the only copy of an input the unread file could not tell us about.

loaded failed -> patch
loaded in flight -> patch
loaded in flight failed -> patch
loaded parked -> patch
loaded parked failed -> patch

loaded parked in flight failed -> patch
not loaded -> patch
not loaded failed -> patch
not loaded in flight -> patch
not loaded in flight failed -> patch
not loaded parked -> patch
not loaded parked failed -> patch
not loaded parked in flight -> patch
not loaded parked in flight failed -> patch
blocked (state.json did not load), loaded nothing outstanding -> none
blocked (state.json did not load), loaded failed -> none
blocked (state.json did not load), loaded in flight -> none
blocked (state.json did not load), loaded in flight failed -> none
blocked (state.json did not load), loaded parked -> none
blocked (state.json did not load), loaded parked failed -> none
blocked (state.json did not load), loaded parked in flight -> none
blocked (state.json did not load), loaded parked in flight failed -> none

retiredKeepNote: R21a / R21b (D-SINK-19 round 11): Model.retiredInputsToKeep(entry, landed) -- which retired keys an owned write leaves on the bar entry. `landed` is whether the state as last confirmed on disk carries the migration marker. Until it does, every retired key the entry carries is KEPT (the URL there may be the only copy of what the migration's state write carries); once it does, NONE is, whatever it holds -- valid, refused, held by a record or not. Anything but the boolean true reads as not landed, so a caller that does not know keeps them. `want` is the keep list in RETIRED_SETTINGS order. R17a's held/consumed cube and R20c's landed-state rule were withdrawn with the route they served.

retiredKeep.name: not landed: a playlist and a guide URL on the entry -> keep both
not landed: a playlist alone -> keep it
not landed: a guide URL alone -> keep it
not landed: a REFUSED value -> kept too (the migration reports and strips it once its write has landed)
not landed: nothing on the entry -> nothing kept
landed: a playlist and a guide URL -> strip both
landed: whitespace-wrapped values -> stripped (no comparison is made at all)
landed: a value a record holds -> stripped
the string "true" is not landed -> keep (fail-safe)
